rc-car-1to10-chassis.name: 1/10 scale custom RC chassis assembly (design dimensions, not a manufacturer product)
rc-car-1to10-chassis.design_basis: Dimensioned so that the sourced parts (Arduino Nano, MG996R, QuicRun 540, QuicRun 1060 ESC, 2S 5200 pack, 59/68 mm tires) physically fit a 1/10 scale layout. Wheelbase and track follow the 1/10 scale class, not any single product.
rc-car-1to10-chassis.uncertainty: Every chassis dimension is a design decision recorded here, not a measurement of a real product. Tire and motor mounting positions are chosen to satisfy the sourced part envelopes; the spring rates, camber, ackermann and tire friction below are design targets with no measured source and must not be read as calibrated.
rc-car-1to10-chassis.physics_uncertainty: tire_mu 1.15 is a design target for a rubber tire on smooth asphalt (published RC on-road tire friction coefficients sit roughly 0.9-1.3). tire_vertical_stiffness 90 kN/m and damping 900 Ns/m are design targets; no measured tire spring rate exists for this carcass. drag 0.62 and frontal area 0.042 m2 are estimates from the body envelope, not from a wind tunnel.
rc-car-1to10-chassis.mass_source: Design target: ~1.18 kg ready-to-run for a 1/10 on-road/buggy (battery 268 g + motor 168 g + ESC 39 g + 55 g servo + electronics ~60 g + chassis/body/tyres the remainder). Not a weighed value.
rc-car-1to10-chassis.inertia_source: Derived from the mass breakdown above combined as point masses at the front and rear axle heights: Ixx uses the mean wheel radius, Izz uses the wheelbase and rear track. No measured inertia exists.

tire.source: Design target for a rubber tire on smooth asphalt; no measured tire data.

aero.source: Estimated from the body envelope in specs/rc-chassis-assembly.json.

drivetrain.source: Gear ratio 50/12 = 4.1667 from the chosen pinion/spur tooth counts; efficiency 0.85 is a design target for a nylon spur gear.

steering.steering_ratio_note: The firmware maps the steering pot to 65-115 deg; the physical steering ratio (servo angle to road-wheel angle) follows from the tie-rod geometry in the assembly spec.

integration_gaps: WireUp's catalog has no brushed DC motor or ESC part, so this profile is not yet driven by any simulated component.
WireUp's catalog has no radio receiver; the current firmware reads two potentiometers directly instead of a PWM receiver frame.
The current firmware steps the L293D as a stepper, so no 0-100% throttle PWM reaches the motor and the ESC cannot be simulated from firmware output yet.
